Alec: :rotating_light: noticing a weird headroom dip in eus4 GPU pool, headroom dropped ~12% in last 6m, p95 queueing up
ops-bot: ALERT eus4-gpu-headroom low threshold breached
ops-bot: metrics snapshot:
```
region: eus4
pool: hosted-gpu-a
headroom_percent: -12.3
p95_queue_ms: 1870
active_pods: 128
capacity_nodes: 130
``` 
Maya: :eyes: is this the regular scheduled refill window? looks off compared to previous days
Cheng: Not during refill window, autoscaler hasn't picked extra nodes. I'm seeing increased small-job churn, maybe many short LLM sessions
Alec: Are admission controls kicking in? any rate-limit logs?
Jen (SRE): admission control logs show increased reject rate from proxy at 1765004450
Jen (SRE): `admission.reject_count_total{region="eus4"}` went from 2/min to 45/min
Maya: Can we temporarily raise reserved headroom to avoid client-facing errors? or route burst traffic to euw1 fallback?
Cheng: Quick check: routing policy 'regional-overspill' enabled, but capacity in euw1 == tight too. We can enable 'burst-remote' to route low-priority to euw2
Alec: Do we want an emergency scale override? I can flip to +4 nodes for hosted-gpu-a (cpu quota ok)
Jen (SRE): Do it, but warn cost owners. Add a note in pager duty channel. Also start a dbg trace on small-job classifier to confirm churn source
Maya: Linking runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-headroom-ops
Alec: flipping override now -> `./infractl scale --region eus4 --pool hosted-gpu-a --delta 4` 
ops-bot: scaling started at 1765004488, target nodes=134, expected join ETA ~2m
Cheng: confirmed extra nodes coming up, p95 queue dropping
Jen (SRE): keep monitoring. Follow-up: schedule a retrospective to identify why autoscaler didn't react to the churn pattern
Maya: I'll open a ticket on backlog with metrics + ktrace
Alec: thanks team, marking as ongoing until healthy. :thumbsup:
